summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-babel ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes opaque bundled payload
details: The package's preinstall hook (setup.mjs) is obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers (_0xNNNN) and per-function string-lookup tables that hide its operations. On npm install it downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, chmods it executable, and uses it to run math_init.js — a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (@bun @bun-cjs header, ~700KB numeric constant array fed to a string decoder hc1jfK9). The payload never executes under Node, evading Node-based tooling, and its contents are not readable as source. An eslint-config package has no legitimate need for an alternate language runtime or an obfuscated bundled payload — a legitimate eslint config is a small declarative JS/JSON file with no install hooks. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern here is used to run attacker-controlled bundled code on the installer's machine at install time. The scope @ornikar and the package name suggest impersonation of a real organization's internal eslint config.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
